hero.headline: How Shake's Payment System Keeps You Safe, Literally

section1.headline: The Escrow Process
section1.description:
The Shake escrow is powered by a smart contract on the Ethereum Base network. Once a payment is made, funds are locked by code — not by Shake, not by a bank, and not by a third party. 

Shake never takes custody of user funds. Payments are held by the smart contract itself, while users transact using their preferred wallet — including Coinbase Embedded Wallet on mobile, Telegram wallet and Tonkeeper on Telegram, or native ETH wallets on Farcaster. Fiat onramp and offramp services are powered by Coinbase on mobile. This design removes single-point-of-failure risk and ensures funds can only move according to the agreed rules.

howItWorks.escrowIntro: Shake uses an escrow which is like a safe that keeps the customer's money secure while a business delivers a product or service.
howItWorks.agreementNote: Any escrow should have an agreement that the buyer and seller both sign before money is exchanged. AI in the app suggests an agreement, and pictures you take are included. Just sign with your finger.
howItWorks.smartContractNote: Under the hood, it's a smart contract on the Ethereum Base network: the lockup rules are written to the blockchain at the moment of payment and cannot be altered by anyone, including Shake. Funds can only be released to the merchant (either upon lockup expiry or via signed early withdrawal after the dispute window closes without dispute) or returned to the buyer if a refund is approved by an arbiter. No other path exists in the code.

process.step1: After making a transaction, your money is placed into an escrow for the agreed duration (0–180 days), which is like a neutral safe, rather than going directly to the merchant.
process.step2: During this waiting period, if you don't receive what you purchased, you can discuss it with the merchant directly or request a refund, which a human reviewer will evaluate.
process.step3: If no dispute is requested during the agreed escrow period, the merchant can withdraw funds immediately, or receive them automatically once the standard arbitration buffer concludes at the baseline fee.

questions.question: How does the app work?
questions.answer: Shake uses smart-contract escrow on the Ethereum Base network, which acts like a safe that keeps the customer's money secure while a business delivers a product or service. To learn more, see the "How it Works" page.

questions.question: How do I get started?
questions.answer:
You can get started across multiple platforms:
- **iOS & Android**: [Download the mobile app](https://shakedefi.com) for full features, Coinbase embedded wallet, and fiat onramp/offramp.
- **Telegram**: Chat with [@ShakeDefiBot](https://t.me/ShakeDefiBot) or open the [Telegram mini-app](https://t.me/ShakeDefiBot/app) to create escrow deals and connect your Telegram wallet or Tonkeeper.
- **Farcaster**: Open the [Shake mini-app on Farcaster](https://farcaster.xyz/miniapps/4LNSH2r_Bkx7/shake-defi) and transact with your native Base ETH wallet.

questions.question: Which platforms and wallets does Shake DeFi support?
questions.answer:
Shake DeFi is available on iOS, Android, Telegram, and Farcaster, supporting:
- **Coinbase Embedded Wallet** (iOS & Android): Full feature access including fiat onramp/offramp and Odos currency swapping.
- **Telegram Wallet & Tonkeeper** (Telegram): Transact with TON and USDT, browse the P2P Marketplace channel, or chat with [@ShakeDefiBot](https://t.me/ShakeDefiBot).
- **Native ETH Wallet** (Farcaster): Transact on the Ethereum Base network directly from your Farcaster client.

Simply copy the listing text to your clipboard and paste it into Shake DeFi — either on the app's Payment screen or in a chat with [@ShakeDefiBot](https://t.me/ShakeDefiBot) on Telegram. Shake automatically parses the details, lets you select your desired cryptocurrency, and invites the seller to join a smart-contract-protected escrow.

questions.question: What is an escrow?
questions.answer:
An escrow is like a safe that keeps the money secure and ensures both the customer and business are fulfilling their obligations before the exchange is made. 

For example, let's say you're buying a used phone from someone you found online. Normally, you'd meet up, pay them on the spot, and hope the phone works. But if it's broken or not what they promised, it's already too late — the money's gone. 

With escrow, instead of paying them directly, your money goes into a secure holding account for a fixed amount of time. The seller sees the money is there, and hands over the phone. 

During the waiting period, you check the quality of the phone. If you discover it's broken, you would dispute the transaction and request a refund. If the phone works, the money is released to the seller once the waiting period is over. 

In essence, the escrow:    
1) Protects businesses by ensuring that the customer's payment is ready and available for transfer once the waiting period is over    
2) Provides protection for both parties by ensuring funds are held securely and can only be released according to the agreed escrow terms, including refunds when warranted by a dispute outcome. 

To learn more, see the "How it Works" page.

questions.question: Do I have to use an escrow period?
questions.answer: No. Merchants can choose any escrow duration from 0 to 180 days, and it can be set to 0 for an instant transfer with no waiting and no refund window. You still get all of Shake's other protections: identity verification, a signed agreement with photos, thorough transaction documentation, and buyer ratings. The escrow period is the right choice when you want to give buyers a safety net — instant transfer is the right choice when the sale is straightforward and both parties are ready.

questions.question: Do I need prior crypto experience or investment knowledge to use Shake?
questions.answer: No prior cryptocurrency experience is required. Shake makes crypto payments as straightforward as everyday payment apps. You don't have to speculate on volatile crypto markets or manage complicated seed phrases — on mobile, you can easily fund your wallet with a debit card or bank account via Coinbase Onramp and transact using price-stable assets like USDC (pegged 1:1 to the US dollar). When you receive funds, you can cash out back to your bank account with Coinbase Offramp. Shake never stores or processes fiat money directly; all escrow transactions settle securely on the blockchain.

questions.question: Who can use the Shake app?
questions.answer: Shake is available for those over the age of 18. Creating a Shake account requires identity verification from the Persona service (withpersona.com).

questions.question: Can I pay with any cryptocurrency I own?
questions.answer:
Yes! Shake supports flexible payment options across supported cryptocurrencies: USDC, ETH, TON, and USDT, plus Bitcoin and Staked ETH via swapping. On mobile, you can transfer cryptocurrency to your Coinbase wallet in the app and convert it using the built-in Odos swap feature. On Telegram, you can pay with TON or USDT via your Telegram wallet or Tonkeeper. On Farcaster, you can transact directly using your native Base ETH wallet.

Note: Coinbase and Odos swap services are not available in all countries.

questions.question: Do I have to accept any 'arbitrary' cryptocurrency as payment?
questions.answer: No, you specify which crypto you want to receive (such as USDC, ETH, TON, or USDT). When buyers pay with a different cryptocurrency like Bitcoin or Staked ETH, they use the built-in swap feature to convert it to your preferred currency before the transaction completes. You always receive exactly what you requested. When withdrawing funds, mobile users can offramp to fiat via Coinbase, while Telegram, Tonkeeper, and Farcaster users receive settled funds directly to their connected wallets.

questions.question: How long does it take to send or accept a payment? Is there an instant transfer fee?
questions.answer: Payments typically confirm on-chain in seconds. The "waiting" you see in Shake isn't transfer time—it's escrow protection. You choose an escrow duration between 0 and 180 days (for example, 3 days, or 0 for instant settlement). During this agreed window, the buyer can inspect the purchase and file a dispute if needed. After that window closes without a dispute, there is a standard 3-day arbitration buffer before automatic release at the baseline 0.1% fee. If a merchant wants to get paid immediately right when the buyer's escrow period ends, they can use early withdrawal for an additional fee (up to 0.9% additional, for a total fee of 1.0%): withdrawing earlier during the buffer incurs 0.4% (1 day early), 0.7% (2 days early), or 1.0% (3 days early). Shake does not charge a separate instant transfer fee; normal network fees may apply.

questions.question: Are there fees to use Shake?
questions.answer:
Shake charges a transparent service fee of just 0.1% – 1% for escrowed transactions. The baseline fee is 0.1% of the transaction amount (for 0-day instant transfers and standard release after the arbitration buffer). 

If a merchant chooses to withdraw funds early once the buyer's dispute window ends, a tiered early withdrawal fee applies (an additional 0.3% to 0.9%, totaling 0.4% to 1.0% depending on how many days early the withdrawal occurs, up to 3 days early). 

Blockchain network fees may also apply, and are paid directly to the network. Currency conversion (fiat ↔ crypto) is handled by Coinbase Onramp and Offramp, which may apply their own fees depending on the asset used. Currency swapping between cryptocurrencies uses the Odos protocol and includes standard swap fees.

Shake does not add hidden fees, does not take custody of funds, and does not charge recurring subscription fees for basic use.

questions.question: Do I need to report my Shake transactions on my taxes?
questions.answer:
In most countries, including the United States, cryptocurrency transactions are taxable events. This applies to Shake transactions as well. There are three main transaction types to be aware of:

1) Paying for goods or services with crypto is treated as a disposal of that asset. If the crypto's value increased since you acquired it, you may owe capital gains tax on the difference.
2) Swapping between cryptocurrencies (e.g., converting Bitcoin to USDC via Shake's built-in swap feature) is also generally treated as a taxable event in the U.S.
3) Receiving crypto as a merchant is typically treated as ordinary income at the fair market value at the time of receipt.

Crypto tax tools like [CoinLedger](https://coinledger.io) and [Koinly](https://koinly.io) make this process straightforward. They can import your on-chain transaction history — including Shake transactions, which are permanently recorded on the blockchain — and automatically calculate your gains, losses, and income.

questions.question: Are there any income requirements to use Shake?
questions.answer: No, there are no income requirements to use Shake.

questions.question: Can I accept international transactions with Shake?
questions.answer: Yes, you can accept international transactions from any other Shake user.

questions.question: In which countries is Shake not available?
questions.answer: Shake is not available in Brazil, Mexico, Taiwan, Japan, and United Kingdom.

questions.question: Are there any spending requirements, limits or transaction caps?
questions.answer: There are no spending limits or transaction caps imposed by Shake itself.

questions.question: What happens if there is a dispute?
questions.answer: Shake's process records metadata and provides transaction information so a human reviewer can resolve disputes fairly. By default, a member of Shake's team reviews the evidence and decides the outcome — no algorithm or smart contract makes that call. Arbiters issue refunds when warranted.

questions.question: How does Shake protect against fraud and unauthorized transactions?
questions.answer: Shake protects against fraud and unauthorized transactions with verified identities, signed agreements for each transaction, and verifiable on-chain proof of payment, backed by detailed records for dispute resolution.

questions.question: Why can't Shake or a hacker take my money and run?
questions.answer:
Shake is non-custodial and never has custody of user funds or private keys. Payments are held by an on-chain smart contract on the Ethereum Base network that can only release funds to the merchant after the escrow period, or back to the buyer in the case of a refund. 

Shake does not store your wallet private keys on any platform. On mobile, Coinbase provides secure embedded wallet infrastructure. On Telegram, keys stay secured in your Telegram wallet or Tonkeeper. On Farcaster, transactions are signed directly with your native ETH wallet. Shake cannot access, move, or redirect escrowed funds. Escrow logic is enforced by blockchain code, not by human discretion — the only human input is the arbiter's dispute decision, which the contract then carries out automatically.

questions.question: What is documented when I make a transaction?
questions.answer: Shake encrypts all data and logs every detail: Time, location, signatures, and photos that you provide. Each party's device also takes a front-facing photo of the signer as they are signing. Delivery confirmation can be uploaded, and the system confirms the money is available before a transaction happens.

questions.question: How does Shake create accountability?
questions.answer: Every Shake user has a verified identity and feedback score. Persona checks each member's ID, so no one can make unlimited wallets to hide from accountability.

questions.question: What information is public?
questions.answer: While transactions are recorded on the blockchain (which is publicly viewable but anonymous), personal Shake accounts and blockchain accounts are not publicly associated.

questions.question: Is there support for splitting shared expenses amongst a group?
questions.answer: While this isn't currently supported, it is on our roadmap for future implementation.

questions.question: Where is Shake Defi incorporated?
questions.answer: Shake Defi, Inc. is incorporated in Brookfield, Wisconsin, United States .
